research_problem: Select a covalent organic framework with high xenon-over-krypton adsorption selectivity. Each candidate is an actual COF represented by 14 continuous structural and compositional descriptors; search is restricted to the finite material library, so descriptors must not be recombined into fictitious materials.

decision_variables.name: pore_diameter_Å
decision_variables.meaning: Characteristic pore diameter in angstrom. Confinement and molecular accessibility strongly affect Xe/Kr adsorption selectivity.

decision_variables.name: void_fraction
decision_variables.meaning: Fraction of the crystal volume accessible as void space.

decision_variables.name: surface_area_m²g⁻¹
decision_variables.meaning: Gravimetric internal surface area in square metres per gram.

decision_variables.name: crystal_density
decision_variables.meaning: Bulk crystal density descriptor supplied by the source dataset.

objective.name: negative_high_fidelity_gcmc_xe_kr_selectivity
objective.definition: The hidden high-fidelity mixture GCMC calculation returns Xe/Kr adsorption selectivity. This benchmark uses obj = -selectivity, so smaller is better.
objective.selectivity_definition: Xe/Kr selectivity compares the adsorbed Xe/Kr ratio with the feed Xe/Kr ratio.

public_scientific_knowledge: Xe is larger and more polarizable than Kr, so sufficiently confining pores and stronger dispersion interactions can favor Xe adsorption.
Very open structures with large pores and high void fraction can reduce confinement-driven selectivity even when they offer high capacity.
Pore diameter, void fraction and crystal density are coupled geometric descriptors; no single descriptor is guaranteed globally monotonic.
Surface area often affects adsorption capacity more directly than binary selectivity.
Element-density descriptors can alter adsorption interactions, but their effects depend on chemical environment and pore geometry; they should be treated as uncertain modifiers.

candidate_protocol.full_search_pool: 608 actual COFs from the published benchmark.
candidate_protocol.visible_candidates: all rows supplied in input/candidates.csv for the current run
candidate_protocol.comparison_pairs: all rows supplied in input/pairs.tsv for the current run
candidate_protocol.candidate_identity_policy: COF names are withheld from the Agent to prevent lookup of published target rankings; the 14 benchmark descriptors are visible.

simulator.kind: hidden high-fidelity mixture GCMC result table

available_information: The complete 14D descriptor vector for every visible candidate.
Descriptor meanings, observed library ranges and fixed GCMC conditions.
The scientific objective and its conversion to minimization.
unavailable_information: COF identities, CIF structures and all GCMC/Henry output values.
Candidate selectivity/objective values and true pair labels.
Optimization histories, previously fitted response models and the published best-material identity.
agent_task: Use adsorption and porous-material knowledge to estimate which descriptor vector should have the smaller negative Xe/Kr selectivity objective. Treat pore accessibility, confinement and chemistry as interacting hypotheses; abstain when the direction is not robust.
